summary: Email-verified sign-up (register -> code -> verify) tested end-to-end: 12/14 pytest cases passed; 2 failed only because of an upstream Emergent/Resend 'rate_limited' response hit after many sends in this iteration (code logic is correct and rolls back last_sent_at on failure). All frontend verify-email UI pieces render and behave correctly on 390x844 (register toasts, 6 code boxes, resend countdown, wrong-code error with tries-left, change-email navigation). Legacy accounts (trader@optiscreen.app, lingesa4@gmail.com) still log in with 200. Pending-email login returns 403 and login.tsx routes to verify-email as designed.

minor.issue: When Emergent email proxy responds 429 with code 'rate_limited', emailer.py falls through to generic 502 'We couldn't send the email'. Consider mapping 'rate_limited' into the same pause-list as 'insufficient_credits'/'daily_limit_reached' and return 503 'Email is temporarily unavailable'. Reference: /app/backend/emailer.py:115 (code tuple).

action_items: Optional polish: in /app/backend/emailer.py add 'rate_limited' to the code tuple that maps to HTTP 503 so users get a 'temporarily unavailable' message instead of a 502 bad-gateway when Resend rate limit kicks in.

No functional fixes required — all specified flows (register 202, pending-login 403, resend cooldown 429 -> 202 after cooldown with reset attempts & new digest, old code invalidated on resend, verify wrong-code countdown 4/3/2/1 then lockout, 422 for non-6-digit, 400 expired, 200 on correct code with user created & pending doc deleted, 404 on reuse, /auth/me with token, follow-up login, legacy logins unaffected, re-register in cooldown preserves same digest and refreshes password) are working.
critical_code_review_comments: signup.py correctly rolls back last_sent_at on email send failure so users can retry immediately — good resilience.
code_digest is HMAC(JWT_SECRET, email:code) and never stored in plain text — matches the credential contract.
verify-email.tsx hidden TextInput is layered under 6 boxes via a Pressable (good UX); testIDs on all key elements.

success_rate.backend: 86% (12/14 — 2 upstream email rate-limit failures, not code bugs)
success_rate.frontend: 100% on the flows exercised (register toast, verify screen render, 6 boxes, resend timer, wrong-code error, change-email)

seed_data_creation: All test accounts used delivered+uitest*@resend.dev. Cleaned up email_verifications and users for those addresses at the end of the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Emergent/Resend email proxy applies a rate limit (observed around 6 sends per hour per domain). Space signup/resend tests out and only use delivered+<label>@resend.dev addresses. Use the HMAC overwrite trick (hmac(JWT_SECRET, '<email>:<code>')) to inject a known code into email_verifications.code_digest instead of sending more emails. The response contract from /auth/register is {verification_required, email, resend_in, expires_in, attempts_left} (no session_token until /auth/register/verify).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs introduced. The 2 failing tests were caused by upstream Resend 'rate_limited' responses because many signup emails had already been sent in this environment (previous iterations + this run). The signup.issue_code function correctly resets last_sent_at on upstream failure (/app/backend/signup.py:107-110), so clients can retry immediately once the limit lifts.
